Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime — redistributed with Z Privacy for Windows
=======================================================================

Three files in this folder beside zprivacy.exe are Microsoft's, not ours:

  vcruntime140.dll
  vcruntime140_1.dll
  msvcp140.dll

They are the Visual C++ runtime that any program built with Microsoft's C++
compiler needs in order to start — and a Windows machine does not always have
it. On a clean installation, Z Privacy would otherwise stop with Windows' own
dialogue about a missing DLL before it drew anything.

**Why they travel with the application rather than being installed.** The
other way is to run Microsoft's `vc_redist.x64.exe`, which installs the
runtime for the whole machine and asks for an administrator. Z Privacy's
installer promises neither: it installs for one person, into that person's own
folder, with no administrator prompt. So the three files are copied beside the
application — Microsoft calls this «app-local deployment» — and the Windows
loader finds them there. **Nothing is installed system-wide, and nothing on
the machine changes outside the application's own folder.**

**The permission.** Microsoft's Visual Studio redistribution terms allow these
files to be distributed with an application built with their tools; the list of
redistributable files is published by Microsoft with the toolset (`redist.txt`
in the Visual C++ redistributable folder of the build machine). The copies in
this release come from the build machine's own Visual Studio installation, from
the folder its `VCToolsRedistDir` names, so they are the versions that compiler
expects.

The file version each copy carries is printed in the build log of the run that
made this release, and `BUILD-INFO.txt` beside this folder names that run's
commit.

These three files are redistributed unmodified. Everything about Z Privacy
itself — its licence, its source, its obligations — is in the files beside this
one.
